items.title: An update on independent evaluators
items.detailText:
Anthropic announces updates to embedding independent evaluators
Last month, we committed to stronger independent, third-party assessment of our models and safety practices. We also signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, in which companies pledged to partner with independent external auditors or evaluators. Today, we’re announcing that we’ve started to give employee-like access to a team from METR , a nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models.
METR will publish the results of its risk assessments. Over the past year, we’ve worked with METR on several reviews of our Risk Reports . We’re also working with SecureBio and Accenture as evaluators, and are in early discussions with several other organizations, including Hugging Face .
Here, we explain our approach to working with evaluators.
To evaluate frontier models, evaluators need the following:
Although the analogy isn’t exact, bank supervision operates on similar logic. Banks know more about their own risk positions than outsiders do, so regulators assign resident examiners to work inside the largest banks. If a bank’s risk-taking could threaten the public, third parties try to see that in advance.
For the AI industry, this is a step toward robust safety oversight . We’re moving quickly with multiple evaluators and learning actively about what kinds of partnership work. We’re committed to sharing updates as we go.
We’ve onboarded six METR employees with company hardware, office space, and access to internal tools and systems that are roughly on par with what our own risk assessment teams have access to. Outside a small number of clearly defined categories (e.g., data about customers, attorney-client privileged information, or information about our model architectures), Anthropic employees are encouraged to share information with them just as they would with a fellow employee working on alignment risk. 1
METR will publish its analysis of our risk levels, incidents, or practices. Anthropic can’t veto publication, but we can require them to redact information if it falls into predefined categories such as reproducing confidential IP. (Anthropic ultimately decides what information does and does not fall into these categories, although METR reserves the right to make certain statements about the level of access and information it received.) 2
Our engagement with METR is limited to a small team operating under enforceable agreements. Other METR employees are siloed from that team’s work, including researchers who work with us on other projects. Embedded evaluation gives a few qualified people working under Anthropic’s security standards a close view of how we operate. It’s not a way for other organizations to obtain our information, or that of our customers and partners.

items.title: Anthropic has opened an office in Singapore and signed an MOU with the country’s government to advance safe, responsible AI adoption.
items.detailText:
Anthropic opens its fifth Asia-Pacific office in Singapore and signs an MOU with the government on AI safety, evaluation, and responsible adoption.
“We’re committed to Singapore for the long term,” said Dale Finlay, General Manager of ASEAN at Anthropic. “Our customers here hold AI to an extremely high standard, especially when it comes to reliability and security. Having a team on the ground means we can get even closer to the organizations putting Claude to work on their hardest problems.”
“Singapore has been a leader in responsible AI, with a long track record of investment in model testing and evaluation,” said Mann. “We founded Anthropic on the belief that capability and safety have to go hand in hand. With this MOU, we’ll partner with Singapore to help ensure the transition to powerful AI goes well here, across Asia-Pacific, and around the world.”
“Singapore’s approach to AI has always been to enable innovation while keeping pace with its evolving risks. Trust is critical for businesses, workers, and the public to use AI with confidence,” said Chng. “This partnership with Anthropic reflects the Government’s commitment to scaling up the responsible adoption of AI, deepening capabilities in our companies and government agencies, and delivering impact for Singapore.”
Our work with Singapore goes back to 2023, when we joined the Generative AI Evaluation Sandbox run by the Infocomm Media Development Authority and the AI Verify Foundation. We later partnered with them on a red-teaming project in English, Mandarin, Malay, and Tamil.
Under the MOU, we plan to hold technical exchanges with Singapore’s AI safety, security, and assurance institutions on model evaluation, testing standards, and incident response. We do similar work with safety institutes around the world, where sharing technical information provides governments with a clearer view of frontier AI capabilities and risks, while helping developers build safer models.
We’ll also look for ways to strengthen AI skills in Singapore, help small and medium-sized businesses adopt AI responsibly, and support the government’s goal of building AI capability among public officers. We plan to share research and data with the government, including from the Anthropic Economic Index , and to offer technical and policy expertise as Singapore develops its rules for AI.
In our latest Economic Index , Singapore ranks second of 121 countries in Claude.ai usage relative to its population, at nearly six times what its size alone would predict.

items.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
items.detailText:
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
Today we’re launching the Anthropic Cyber Mission, a long-term commitment to securing the systems everyone depends on. The Cyber Mission is a new effort to support defenders with tools, research, and resources to secure their software and systems. We’re starting with two areas:
Today, we’re introducing the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program , which brings frontier Claude models, on-site engineers, and our threat research to those trusted providers. Its founding partners are Accenture, Booz Allen, CrowdStrike, Deloitte, Dragos, Hitachi, Insane Cyber, Nozomi Networks, Palo Alto Networks, PwC, and Rockwell Automation.
These organizations represent the providers that operators rely on to secure these systems: the consulting and advanced technology companies that run security programs, the security companies that guard the business and industrial networks, and the manufacturers that build and patch the equipment itself.
This work is underway. Several partners are currently working with Claude to fix vulnerabilities and help customers do the same. Critical infrastructure is hard to defend in many ways that AI cannot fix, but we believe that frontier models can help find and repair weaknesses before those weaknesses are used to cut off power or make water unsafe. Our first step is to work with a small cohort of providers to learn which strategies are most effective and practical.
If your company builds security products or services for critical infrastructure, you can register your interest here .
“ As AI continues to advance, it presents an important opportunity to strengthen cybersecurity across critical infrastructure, provided it is applied responsibly, validated rigorously, and deployed with safety and reliability at the forefront. We are pleased to contribute our operational technology and industrial cybersecurity expertise to help develop practical approaches for applying AI in ways that strengthen the resilience of the infrastructure society depends on every day. ”

“ Through our work with critical infrastructure organizations, PwC’s cyber OT practice has seen firsthand the gravity of consequences cyber breaches can have in these environments. items.title: 巨型AI企业，该以什么样的姿态，走进公开资本市场？
items.detailText:
巨型AI企业，该以什么样的姿态，走进公开资本市场？
曾任职OpenAI研究副总裁的Dario Amodei（达里奥·阿莫代伊）联合创办Anthropic，公司凭借Claude大模型跻身全球顶尖AI企业。
Anthropic冲击IPO的消息传出来，多数人的目光都落在它的收入增速、模型能力，还有万亿估值预期上。很少有人留意到它这套不同于硅谷常规模式的治理结构安排。
这也难怪，硅谷科技公司上市，控制权玩法向来有固定模板，大多是AB股双层股权，把投票权攥在创始人手里。
Anthropic 没有采用传统模式，反而采用公共利益公司（Public Benefit Corporation，PBC）叠加长期独立信托的架构。
这样，Anthropic 公司权力既不在创始人手里，也不在投资人手里，交到一群不持股份、不分利润的外部受托人手上，前美联储主席伯南克就在这个受托人名单里。
投资人手里的股权，价值是不是已经悄悄打了折？这不是一个纸上谈兵的法律问题，是Anthropic这次上市，摆在华尔街面前实打实的考验。
在美国资本市场，绝大多数科技企业采用的是传统商业公司形式，也就是 C Corp。
对于这类传统公司，法律有一条硬性要求：管理层和董事会做重大决策，首要目标必须是让股东赚到更多钱。如果管理层出于安全、社会影响等考量，放弃短期高额利润，股东完全可以起诉董事会，追责赔偿。
公共利益公司（ PBC：Public Benefit Corporation）同样是盈利企业，可以正常融资、发放股权，未来也能上市分红，和普通商业公司一样参与市场竞争。
Anthropic 整套治理架构，由两层体系叠加而成。一层是作为法律载体的公共利益公司，另一层是掌握实际控制权的长期利益信托，二者搭配，构成这套非常特殊的约束机制。
在 PBC 的规则之下，管理层做决定的时候，不必一味优先追逐股东收益，可以合法地把公共安全、社会影响纳入权衡范围。
其实，这种企业形式并不是 Anthropic 首创。户外品牌 Patagonia、众筹平台 Kickstarter、冰淇淋品牌 Ben & Jerry’s，都早早选用了 PBC 架构。
放眼全球顶级 AI 赛道，头部企业在公司架构的选择上走出了三条截然不同的道路，以 OpenAI、Anthropic、xAI 三家为例，差异尤为鲜明。
明星公司 OpenAI 对外商业化运营的主体，注册身份同样是 PBC。OpenAI 采用特殊架构：非营利基金会居于顶层掌握控制权，下设盈利子公司开展商业化，以此约束资本逐利行为。
与 OpenAI 相比，Anthropic 的路线更为折中。二者看似都是为了限制资本，但底层架构存在本质区别。
OpenAI 顶层是非营利基金会；而 Anthropic 主体仍是盈利属性的公共利益公司（Public Benefit Corporation，PBC）。
Anthropic 只是把公司控制权剥离出来，交给独立信托的外部受托人。OpenAI 基金会直接持有股权，Anthropic 的信托并不持有股份，只掌握投票控制权。
2023年，埃隆・马斯克创立 xAI，初衷便是对标 OpenAI。这家公司曾短暂注册为 PBC，之后却选择放弃，转回普通商业公司架构。
xAI 卸下这套附加的使命约束，所有决策围绕商业增长展开，资本操作灵活，扩张速度不受制度限制，安全底线依靠企业自律，没有来自法律和信托层面的硬性约束。
Anthropic 卡在两者中间。它保留市场化融资通道，不会像 OpenAI 那样被非营利主体捆住手脚；同时依托独立信托这套机制，把安全使命转化为硬约束，减少资本短期化冲动压倒长期风险管控的可能。
Anthropic 试图平衡两件很难兼容的事：商业扩张的自由度，和 AI 技术附带的公共责任。
这种分化，藏着行业底层分歧：超级大模型，究竟是一门普通生意，还是带有基础设施属性、自带公共风险的技术？不一样的判断，催生了完全不一样的公司制度。
实际上，大模型的技术风险具备很强外溢性，如果盲目推进商业化，会衍生一系列社会层面风险。
倘若采用普通商业公司的治理框架，资本很容易倒逼管理层，为了短期财报表现放开模型权限、落地高风险业务。PBC 从法律层面给董事会留出了空间，允许其将 AI 安全置于短期利润之上。
但 Anthropic 判断，仅有 PBC 并不足够。PBC 只能在法律上保护董事会，却难以阻挡股东或创始人在巨大商业诱惑下调整发展方向。为此，公司额外增设 LTBT 长期独立信托，构建起双重约束机制。
PBC 仅仅是法律载体，单凭它无法实现对资本的约束。真正手握实权、也最富争议的，是 LTBT 长期利益信托。
受托人团队由外部遴选的专家构成，不持有 Anthropic 股权，无法享受上市增值，也不参与企业分红，酬劳仅用来覆盖时间成本。
受托人拥有两项核心权力：其一，有权更换董事会多数成员，掌握人事层面的核心话语权；其二，当公司发生大额非常规举债、出售半数以上股权、转让达到阈值的核心 AI 模型等重大交易时，必须提前五天向信托报备。
不少商事法律学者研究相关条款后指出，这五天报备并非简单通知，落地后会形成软性否决权。
这和 AB 股模式存在本质差异：AB 股依靠创始人掌握高投票权，权力仍保留在公司内部；而 Anthropic 将这项核心权力，交给了独立于股东与创始团队之外的第三方。
这套架构，已经在机构内部形成完全对立的两种看法，一级和二级市场的容忍度，差别尤其明显。
看多的逻辑很清晰。信托作为第三方守门人，能够避开硅谷公司常见的控制权争斗、创始人与投资方的内耗，保障战略连续性。
在全球AI监管持续收紧的趋势里，自带安全约束的治理结构，本身就是一层合规护城河。资本很难倒逼团队为了季度报表去冒技术风险，研发投入、安全评估这类慢变量，能够持续拿到资源。
一级市场的机构，更愿意为这种长期叙事买单。二级市场的顾虑同样现实，也是未来股价最大的不确定性来源。
最核心的矛盾，是股东权利出现结构性稀释。投资者买入股票，却很难对足以改变公司命运的交易施加影响。
重大事项的开关，握在一群不对股东负责的受托人手里。一旦信托基于安全理由否决一笔可以带来巨大收益的并购、授权方案，股东只能被动接受这个结果，缺少有效的制衡手段。
传统尽调，可以核算收入、毛利率、竞争格局，但市场没法针对受托人的主观判断搭建估值模型。
这里催生一个绕不开的悖论：公司拥有顶级的技术、高速增长的业务，集齐高成长标的全部特质，但股权承载的权利并不完整。市场最终会针对这部分权利缺损，给出折价。
一级市场押注长期空间，可以容纳这个折价；二级市场资金大多带着明确考核周期，对这种不确定的治理风险，态度天然更谨慎。
短期来看，AI行情热度足够高，稀缺性会盖住治理

items.title: 为了算力，扎克伯格要把自由现金流烧干
items.detailText:
坚定烧钱。
美国当地时间10月21日，Meta发布了2026年第三季度财报。公司单季营收同比增长26%，达到646.01亿美元；但在大规模基础设施投入下，自由现金流降至负21.2亿美元，而去年同期为正106.25亿美元。
公司创始人、首席执行官马克·扎克伯格表示投资正在见效，首席财务官苏珊·李（Susan Li）更明确指出，2027年公司仍将继续加大投资力度。Meta在财报中还公布了全新的无投票权C类股方案，试图为跨年度的投资预留资本与治理空间。
对Meta来说，激进的投资已经是必然趋势，眼下的关键不只是广告业务能否继续增长，也包括新增投入能否带来足够的收入与效率提升，以覆盖不断扩大的基础设施成本。
第三季度，Meta实现总营收646.01亿美元，较去年同期的512.42亿美元同比增长26%。不按照美国通用会计准则，若剔除1.13亿美元的外汇逆风影响，固定汇率下的营收增速同样为26%。
这一增长主要由核心广告业务推动，当季广告收入达到630.61亿美元，较去年同期的500.82亿美元增长26%。
应用家族的其他收入为10.97亿美元，推动应用家族总营收达到641.58亿美元。专注于元宇宙与硬件的Reality Labs部门营收则为4.43亿美元。
在流量端，应用家族每日活跃人数达到36.4亿人，同比增长3%。广告展示量同比增长10%，单条广告平均价格上涨14%，平台广告变现能力继续增强。
管理层将这一表现与AI推荐系统的改进联系起来，认为AI正在帮助提升用户参与度和广告投放效率。
第三季度，Meta在财报中计入了98.9亿美元的青少年心理健康相关诉讼和解费用。受此影响，合并营业利润降至129.88亿美元，同比下降37%；报告净利润为98.60亿美元，摊薄后每股收益3.83美元。
就在财报公布的10月21日当天，美国新墨西哥州地区法院法官弗朗西斯·马修针对该州起诉Meta误导消费者数据隐私一案作出判决，判令Meta向该州支付高达 250亿美元的赔偿罚款。
根据官方披露的数据，第三季度Meta经营活动现金流为327.86亿美元，高于去年同期的299.99亿美元。
而在支出端，当季购买物业和设备的现金支出升至339.42亿美元，去年同期为188.29亿美元。如果再加上9.64亿美元的融资租赁本金支付，相关现金支出合计达到了349.06亿美元。
按照Meta官方数据计算，当期自由现金流降至负21.20亿美元。相比之下，2025年第三季度的自由现金流为正106.25亿美元，前九个月累计自由现金流也从去年同期的295.08亿美元收窄至110.49亿美元。
自由现金流转负并不意味着公司出现流动性危机。Meta当季经营活动现金流仍保持在327.86亿美元的高位，自由现金流转负主要反映出资本支出增长速度超过了经营现金流的增长。
截至三季度末，公司的物业及设备净额已从2025年底的1764.0亿美元增至2532.22亿美元，长期债务也从587.44亿美元增至809.22亿美元。
未来的关键，是Meta经营现金流能否持续增长，以及新增资产能否逐步转化为收入与利润。
对于四季度业绩，公司预计营收将在730亿至760亿美元之间，指引中点为745亿美元，相比三季度环比增长约15.3%。
随着资源重新分配，Reality Labs部门的亏损预计将有所控制，2026全年亏损预计降至180亿至190亿美元，2027年预计进一步收窄至150亿美元左右。
在资本开支方面，Meta将2026全年资本支出指引下限上调50亿美元，更新为1350亿至1450亿美元。首席财务官苏珊·李明确指出，虽然2027年预算尚在制定，但公司预计仍将继续保持激进的投资节奏。
短期来看，AI对推荐算法和广告投放效率的提升，正在为核心广告业务带来增量收入。中期来看，三季度推出的个人AI助手Muse及前沿模型Muse Wonder，正在逐步测试订阅模式与开发者接口，探索企业服务和交易场景的商业化方向。长期来看，Meta希望通过超级智能实验室和算力基础设施建设，提升内部运营效率，并开辟新的商业化机会。
管理层表示，尽管前沿AI技术的投资回报周期相对较长，但随着技术积累和产品迭代，公司对保持整体营收增长持乐观态度。
为了配合基础设施建设和长期战略布局，Meta在财报中公布了公司治理与资本结构的调整计划，董事会已批准设立全新的无投票权C类普通股。
根据披露的方案，公司拟向现有A类和B类股东按每1股派发1股C类股的形式发放股票股息。
公司表示，派发C类股不会改变现有股东的投票权结构。公司特别委员会已与扎克伯格签署相关协议，旨在延续现有的治理安排。
2014年，谷歌母公司Alphabet通过按比例派发无投票权C类股的形式完成了拆股，使创始人拉里·佩奇和赛吉·布林在后续持续发行股票用于员工股权激励与并购的同时，成功锁定了公司的控制权。
无投票权的C类股将主要用于Meta未来的员工股权激励、潜在战略收购或其他资本运作。股票股息本身并不会直接为公司带来新的现金流。这一安排体现出Meta希望在维持现有控制权结构的前提下，模仿其他科技巨头成熟的资本工具，为未来的股权激励和资本运作预留空间。
对于需要多年持续投入的AI策略而言，稳定的治理结构有助于管理层推进长期规划，但实际效果仍取决于后续的资本使用效率与投资回报。
Meta的第三季度财报呈现出两条同时向前的曲线，广告业务继续创造收入，AI基础设施则不断扩大资本需求。广告收入增长提供了资金基础，但并不意味着AI 投入必然获得相应回报。
Meta已经明确表示，2027年仍将继续加大投入。对扎克伯格而言，坚持长期战略只是第一步，随着投入继续扩大，公司需要证明，AI带来的新增收入与效率提升，足以支撑这场持续多年的基础设施扩张。
第三季度，我们的应用家族每天有36.4亿人使用，Facebook和Instagram的参与度均创历史新高。Threads月活跃用户已超越X，WhatsApp消息量也创下新高。
我们正在快速推进“为每个人提供个人超级智能”的目标，Muse个人智能体的发布非常成功。在美加地区上线仅一个半月，设置用户就已突破1000万，其中约25%的用户每天都在使用。最常见的用例是购物（占比超25%，平均消费额超200美元）。
由于首周交易量远超预期，我们不得不与Stripe合作临时提高信用额度。接下来，Muse将从下个月开始登陆Meta智能眼镜。

items.title: Critical Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities Disclosed in PHP: Alibaba Cloud’s Quick Protection Guide
items.description: Critical Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities Disclosed in PHP: Alibaba Cloud’s Quick Protection Guide This article introduces the severe PHP RCE vulnerability and Alibaba Cloud's rapid release of a protection guide. CloudSecurity <im
items.detailText:
This article introduces the severe PHP RCE vulnerability and Alibaba Cloud's rapid release of a protection guide.
On October 21, 2026, Alibaba Cloud Security detected PHP’s official disclosure of two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both with a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2. The vulnerability incident is also known as php2shell . Under certain conditions, unauthenticated attackers can craft malicious requests to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the web worker process. Official PHP announcement
PHP is widely used in websites, content management systems, and enterprise applications. Successful exploitation could result in data breaches, website defacement, and service disruptions. Alibaba Cloud Security recommends that affected customers immediately assess their environments, upgrade to a patched version as soon as possible, and keep WAF or Cloud Firewall protection enabled during remediation to reduce business risk .
When PHP handles an out-of-memory (OOM) condition, execution may be interrupted before internal request data has been fully initialized. Subsequent request cleanup may access this invalid data, potentially resulting in remote code execution. PHP has confirmed unauthenticated remote code execution over HTTP in Apache mod_php environments. Exploitation can occur before application code begins executing. Vulnerability details
PHP recommends promptly updating all PHP deployments that handle web requests, including Apache mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed environments. Apache mod_php environments face particularly elevated risk. Official risk advisory
The affected and patched versions for both vulnerabilities across supported stable branches are listed below:
PHP 8.1 and earlier versions have reached the end of standard official security support. Some distributions and long-term support (LTS) providers may offer backported security patches. Contact your vendor to confirm whether both vulnerabilities have been addressed, or upgrade to a supported, patched version. When using distribution packages, determine patch status based on the vendor’s advisories and package revision numbers. Official upgrade guidance
To address these vulnerabilities, customers can use Security Center to inventory PHP assets and monitor host risks, Web Application Firewall to strengthen protection at application entry points, Cloud Firewall to control network access, and Managed Security Service to support investigation and response. While upgrading, confirm that the relevant business assets and traffic are covered by the appropriate protections to minimize coverage gaps.

items.title: The Better Harness Evaluation Model Used by 100,000 Users Is Now Open Source
items.description: The Better Harness Evaluation Model Used by 100,000 Users Is Now Open Source This article introduces the open-source release of Better Harness, a toolkit for evaluating and optimizing AI coding agent workflows based on actual task execution
items.detailText:
This article introduces the open-source release of Better Harness, a toolkit for evaluating and optimizing AI coding agent workflows based on actual task execution.
Recently, we built Better Harness into Qoder Desktop. Since its launch, many users have asked: will this feature be open source?
Today, we’re officially open-sourcing Better Harness. Find the project at: https://github.com/QoderAI/better-harness
Better Harness is an open-source toolkit for analyzing and continuously improving coding agent workflows. It connects the engineering practices, evaluation models, and runtime capabilities of Harness Engineering and Loop Engineering, with support for Claude Code, Codex, Qoder, and Cursor.
All four platforms share the same evaluation model, but they do not yet offer full parity in session analysis, evidence coverage, or output capabilities. The Qoder integration has been repeatedly validated in real development workflows and is currently the most complete reference implementation.
Once you have installed or loaded it on your platform, run the following command in the project you want to analyze:
You can start it now and review the report as you continue reading. If a type of evidence is unavailable, Better Harness explicitly preserves that limitation in its results rather than substituting configuration counts or data from another platform.
Suppose an agent changes a module, runs a test command, and declares the task complete. The real question is not whether the repository “has tests,” but whether that test is relevant to the change, covers the main risks, and produces results that justify handing over the work.
That is why Better Harness does not treat the presence of AGENTS.md, Rules, Skills, MCP, Hooks, Memory, tests, or CI as proof that they actually contributed to the task. Every proposed improvement—a Finding—must include traceable evidence, a concrete impact on the user, the smallest necessary fix scope, and a way to verify the fix.
Here is a snapshot of Better Harness analyzing its own project in Codex:
The report does not equate “missing Codex host tests” with “Codex has failed.” Instead, it preserves the distinction between tests that have not been run and evidence of failure. Scores only help locate issues; what matters is the conclusion, its impact, the smallest necessary fix scope, and how to verify the fix.
This is what separates Better Harness from a configuration checklist. A checklist tells you what a project has; Better Harness examines whether those capabilities actually helped the agent complete a task with trustworthy results.
And if the report’s judgments are to be inspected, revised, and verified again, open source has to mean more than a runnable entry point.

items.title: Qoder Cloud Agents Help Developers Enter the Personal Agent Era
items.description: Qoder Cloud Agents Help Developers Enter the Personal Agent Era This article introduces Qoder Cloud Agents, a managed platform that simplifies building context-aware Personal Agents. Alibaba Cloud Community
items.detailText:
This article introduces Qoder Cloud Agents, a managed platform that simplifies building context-aware Personal Agents.
In the second half of 2026, Personal Agents are becoming a new focus for the AI industry. OpenAI launched Dots at DevDay 2026, and Meta introduced Muse. This wave of product launches points in the same direction: giving everyone an AI assistant that can keep working on their behalf.
Following the excitement around OpenClaw early in the year and the accelerating adoption of coding and workplace agents, Personal Agents are taking AI collaboration into its next phase: from answering questions and completing individual tasks to delivering results on an ongoing basis.
This shift can be understood in three statements:
Figure 1 · The Evolution of AI Assistant Paradigms
For example, preparing an industry briefing is a one-off task. Remembering your areas of interest, gathering information every week, generating reports and sending them through instant messaging (IM), and promptly alerting you to important developments is ongoing collaboration. To add a new research topic, you only need to send a message—not restate the entire background.
A Personal Agent is an AI assistant that works on an ongoing basis around an individual's needs. Its work continues after the user leaves the chat window, and the next conversation picks up from the progress made previously.
For developers, Personal Agents create many opportunities: turning familiar use cases into assistants that users are willing to entrust with ongoing work. But there is still engineering work between “AI can answer” and “an assistant can keep getting things done.”
Connecting to a model is only part of the work. Before putting an assistant in users' hands, several other questions must be addressed.
Where do tasks run? Searching for information, reading and writing files, and running scripts require tools, dependencies, and an isolated environment. You also need visibility into task progress, the step at which a task failed, and where its output files are stored.
How is knowledge of the user carried forward? A task started in a new week is a new task, but it should still reflect that person's areas of interest. Conversation history, long-term memory, and reference files serve different purposes. Each needs a clear owner and must be connected to the correct execution environment.
How does the assistant fit into the user's daily routine? IM messages must be associated with the right user and assistant, and results returned through the original channel. Recurring tasks require scheduling, authorization, and notifications; they cannot depend on the user manually opening a page each time.

items.detailText:
The speakers explain how to run and autoscale LLM agents in production using Ray, detailing system architecture, control planes, multi-region deployments, and CI/CD pipelines with LLM evals.
A monthly overview of things you need to know as an architect or aspiring architect.
Facilitating the Spread of Knowledge and Innovation in Professional Software Development
Unlock the full InfoQ experience by logging in! Stay updated with your favorite authors and topics, engage with content, and download exclusive resources.
Lily Mara explains how to avoid high-risk software rewrites through incremental FFI refactoring. She shares how engineering teams can replace Python bottlenecks with Rust via PyO3, demonstrating how to achieve dramatic function-level speedups, seamless integration testing, and meaningful infrastructure cost savings without microservice overhead.
In this article series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream.
The speakers discuss transitioning AI agents from local FastAPI prototypes to resilient production systems on Kubernetes using Ray. They share operational insights on RayCluster topology, stateful memory handling, auto-scaling on dynamic traffic, and robust control plane designs, while highlighting critical guardrails, multi-region setups, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation pipelines.
Nathen Harvey shares insights from DORA research on AI adoption in software delivery. He explains why AI acts as an amplifier, how the DORA AI Capabilities Model drives outcomes, and why engineering leaders must evolve beyond bottlenecks like code reviews to achieve sustainable productivity, reduce delivery instability, and empower developers without burning out their teams.
Andrew Martin discusses why AI security is fundamentally tied to Kubernetes security. He shares insights into the evolving AI threat landscape, covering non-deterministic agent behavior, GPU supply chain vulnerabilities, shared compute risks, and practical defense strategies - from prompt firewalling to agentic identity - to help secure cloud-native AI workloads in production environments.

items.title: New Gemini tools for small business owners
items.detailText:
Streamline tasks with the new Gemini business hub. Connect Google apps, generate on-brand visuals, and get financial insights. See what’s new.
New Gemini tools for small business owners
Gemini’s new tools — including a dedicated business landing page — help small business owners free up time and focus on what started their companies: their passion.
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Gemini is launching a new central hub to help small business owners manage tasks, finances, and marketing in one place. You can now connect your existing apps and upload brand guidelines to generate consistent, professional visuals automatically. Look for these new tools to roll out globally in the coming days to help you save time and focus on your business.
Gemini is launching new tools to help small business owners save time and get more done. It can now handle tasks like creating brand visuals, organizing messy financial data, and connecting to other apps. These updates let entrepreneurs focus on their passions instead of boring paperwork. Business owners around the world are already using it to grow their companies and solve tricky problems.
Tens of millions of small business owners are using Gemini today to brainstorm future products, manage customer feedback, and analyze business performance. Today, we’re announcing new tools designed to give these entrepreneurs their time back so they can focus on what started it all: their passion.
We’re introducing a new business landing page designed to help small business owners streamline their daily tasks. From this central hub, they can build their brand, analyze finances, understand customer insights, and more.
We’re also making it easy to connect Gemini to Google tools like Google Business Profile, Google Ads, and Google Workspace, as well as third-party connected apps like Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho, and Xero.
Businesses can now define their brand style in Gemini by uploading their website, brand kit, fonts, or color palettes. When paired with the power of Nano Banana 2.1 (our latest image generation model), Gemini can now deliver end-to-end visual results for new product launches or ongoing marketing campaigns. Gemini retains this visual style, allowing owners to easily generate cohesive, on-brand assets without having to repeatedly upload their style guidelines.
Gemini can turn messy spreadsheets, receipts, and purchase records into clear financial graphics and interactive models in seconds. Instead of decoding numbers on their own, small business owners can receive financial insights in a more natural way.
